name: step_ap214_reread
why: THE VOLUME RE-READ FROM THE FILE, not the size of the file. A STEP written and never reopened is a promise: it exists, it weighs, it opens in any viewer. The only measure that says the GEOMETRY survived the translation is reopening it in SOLIDWORKS and comparing the volume -- and that is what this case does.
_why_the_protocol_is_read_back: `swStepAP` takes 203 or 214 (swconst help page FileSaveAsSTEPOptions.htm), and those values have NO enum in `swconst`: the number is a literal, and a literal is something one believes. The only proof that the 214 asked is the 214 got is the FILE_SCHEMA written inside the file, which for AP214 says «AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN». 242 is not a value of `swStepAP`: written there it gives an AP203 file (Z-C21.13, finding C5-7), and AP242 goes through PublishSTEP242File instead.

expect.why: asked for and obtained are two different things, and here they are compared
it is the name the STANDARD gives to AP214, and it is written inside the file

expect.tolerance_why: it is the volume of the part, read from GetMassProperties which returns cubic metres
as above, but on the TRANSLATED geometry: it is the number that counts
a BREP must lose nothing: the thousandth the operation allows is already ten times this

includes: reopened as a part and closed again

expect.why: the part open is still its own: reopening the STEP must not leave the translated document lying around
